notes: PSA 19 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.33. Prostate volume 58 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.75.

note_sections.t: Clinical reassessment driven by escalating PSA values and histological upgrading observed during the previous prostate biopsy.

A 71-year-old secondary school teacher presents for review. Initial workup for a rising PSA occurred in early 2024, with levels climbing to 19.0 ng/mL subsequent to a radical prostatectomy performed at age 70. He is married yet resides independently, relying on his spouse for primary support. Daily exercise consists of 45-minute walks, alongside a weekly alcohol intake of roughly six units. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms yield an IPSS score of 14/35, though he denies haematuria or skeletal discomfort. A current smoking habit totals 33 pack-years, without associated chronic cough or shortness of breath. Body weight registers at 100 kg, corresponding to a BMI of 34.6. He voices significant apprehension about invasive interventions, preferring extended consultation periods. Past surgical history encompasses a distant appendectomy during his twenties and a right knee meniscectomy. Recent outpatient visits address cataract surveillance by ophthalmology and routine foot care via podiatry. No comorbidities or active medications are reported.

DRE — prostate: symmetrically enlarged, firm nodule (nodus) palpable in the right lobe. General assessment shows stable vitals (BP 116/65 mmHg, HR 77 bpm), absent drug allergies, and no palpable supraclavicular or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
